analysis.title: The global bond reset to a structurally higher yield regime
key_insights: Global bond markets are moving to a structurally higher-yield equilibrium because of persistent fiscal demands, greater capex needs and fading central-bank support, which rebuild term premia.

Base case is a durable high-yield regime, not an uninterrupted rise in yields. Tactical rallies are expected as stretched policy-rate expectations unwind, but long-dated yields should stay volatile and higher for longer.

Policy expectations look too hawkish. 5y3m OIS rates in the US and euro area temporarily rose to around 4.75% and 3.5%, about 100 bps above Generali's neutral-rate estimates. Pricing out this excess tightening should lower yields, especially at shorter maturities.

The term premium is expected to keep rising on inflation uncertainty and bond supply. Generali's model projects roughly +60 bps in the 10-year US term premium over three years, and up to +100 bps if inflation is 0.5 pps higher and the deficit 1.5 pps wider than baseline.
Lower short-end yields combined with higher long-end yields make curve steepening trades the clearest expression of the view.

Fiscal pressure is structural. Ageing, defence spending and the climate transition keep public spending high, and political fragmentation lowers the odds of lasting fiscal adjustment, especially in the US. Wider deficits mean heavier issuance while central banks shrink balance sheets.

Fed Treasury holdings have stabilised at about 21% of GDP and Generali thinks balance-sheet shrinkage is finished. Fed Chair Warsh favoured deeper cuts to holdings in the past and has commissioned a research group on balance-sheet policy. Generali expects no change to balance sheet policy in the medium term.

A shift by the Fed toward a shorter maturity profile in its holdings (first envisaged by Powell and confirmed by Warsh) would force private investors to absorb more long-duration Treasury risk and push term premia higher.

In the euro area the ECB is expected to treat the deposit facility rate as its main policy instrument while APP and PEPP run off passively. Generali expects the ECB to eventually stop QT or set up a new portfolio to keep excess liquidity ample, since the reserve level needed to avoid upward pressure on short rates has risen.

Japan reinforces the global channel. Higher JGB yields have made JGBs more attractive to Japanese investors than FX-hedged foreign bonds, so Japanese net purchases of foreign bonds turned negative in 2026. For euro-based investors the hedged 10-year JGB pick-up over Bunds fell about 70 bps in three years to about 30 bps.
The convenience yield of government bonds is eroding as fiscal uncertainty weakens their perceived safety, which forces issuers to pay higher yields, especially at long maturities.

A higher neutral rate is possible. AI-related productivity gains could lift potential growth and heavier government borrowing keeps capital demand high. AI adoption should be deflationary in the medium term but is hard to time.
Financial repression, such as restarting bond buying or changing bank regulation to favour government securities, is a last-resort option that could complicate inflation fighting.

Strategic duration overweight is premature. Sell-off overshoots can create tactical entry points to add duration. Portfolio returns should rely on carry, selectivity and active management across duration, credit and equities.

Upside risk to yields comes from inflation or fiscal deficit surprises. Downside risks to yields come from financial-stability stress from rising government debt, a sharper growth slowdown, durable disinflation or credible fiscal consolidation.

macro_indicators.interpretation: About 100 bps above Generali's neutral-rate estimate and judged too high. Pricing out the excess should lower yields, mostly at shorter maturities.
About 100 bps above Generali's neutral-rate estimate and judged too high. Short-end yields have room to decline.

macro_indicators.reading: +60 bps expected rise (up to +100 bps in the adverse case)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Rising term premium should offset easing in policy-rate expectations, keeping long-end yields higher and volatile.
Generali sees the balance-sheet shrinkage as finished, which removes some upward pressure on rates.
Seen as consistent with the ECB's desired short-term rate level, but further declines could push short-term rates up.

macro_indicators.indicator: Hedged 10-year JGB yield pick-up over Bunds (euro-based investor)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Down about 70 bps in three years, which reduces the incentive for foreign investors to buy JGBs and weakens demand for global bonds.

trade_ideas.description: Curve steepening trades in US and euro area government bonds (lower short-end yields, higher long-end yields)
trade_ideas.rationale: Stretched policy-rate expectations leave room for short-end yields to fall while rising term premium limits long-end downside.
trade_ideas.risk: Inflation or fiscal deficit surprises could cause a renewed sell-off; sharper growth slowdown, durable disinflation or credible fiscal consolidation could lower long-end yields.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically add duration when sell-offs overshoot, with no strategic duration overweight
trade_ideas.rationale: Overshoots can create entry points to capture rebounds, but structural forces prevent yields from returning to the previous cycle's lows.
trade_ideas.risk: Duration risk remains despite higher starting yields.

risk_factors: Inflation or fiscal deficits surprising to the upside could trigger a renewed bond sell-off.
Rising debt-servicing costs create a negative loop that makes deficit reduction harder.
Financial-stability pressure from high and rising government debt.
A much sharper growth slowdown or durable disinflation could push yields lower.
Balance-sheet changes that shorten the maturity profile of Fed holdings would raise term premia.
Reduced Japanese demand for foreign bonds and weaker foreign demand for JGBs.
ECB excess liquidity falling below the needed threshold could push up short-term money market rates.
Recurring supply shocks and geopolitical fragmentation raise inflation volatility.
vol_and_positioning: Long-dated yields are expected to stay volatile as term premia rise.
Curve-steepening trades are preferred: short-end yields have downside, long-end yields have upside from term premium.
geopolitical: A durable resolution of the Middle East conflict would lower energy prices and inflation pressure, reinforcing the scenario of lower short-end yields.
Geopolitical fragmentation and instability threaten more volatile inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Bond rally case: stretched policy-rate expectations (5y3m OIS about 100 bps above neutral) unwind, a Middle East resolution lowers energy prices, and growth disappoints, pushing yields lower, especially at the short end.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising term premium (+60 bps over three years, up to +100 bps) from fiscal pressure, bond supply, inflation uncertainty, QT and reduced Japanese demand keeps long-end yields higher and volatile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Higher-yield view is invalidated by a much sharper growth slowdown, durable disinflation, credible fiscal consolidation or financial-stability stress from government debt; a sell-off view is reinforced by upside inflation or deficit surprises.
